lastText: File ClosedFewer Divisions, Fully ArmedMinor VictorySoviet High Command, 1941 — 1945End of hostilities: MARCH 1945 (PROJECTED)Immediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around March 1945 — earlier than the historical May 1945, bought with a faster, costlier advance. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over — a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The industrial evacuation was subordinated to front supply in 1941 — easing that autumn's crisis at a cost in Urals production capacity that every later year of this campaign quietly pays for. The drive on Rostov closed the door on Army Group A — the encirclement history reached for and missed, landed on this path at the favorable edge of what the winter logistics allowed. The push straight for Berlin in February was actually attempted here — testing Chuikov's postwar claim against the flank risk Zhukov's own staff warned about, rather than leaving the question a memoir argument. No branch of this campaign reaches a different destination — only the timing and the price were ever in Soviet hands.One Year LaterVictory arrived ahead of the historical May 1945, which means the occupation of eastern and central Europe has had that much longer to harden by the time this account picks back up a year later.
